significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the conclusion that backtracking follows an ordered detector-then-reroute mechanism in which an "error/inconsistency detector writes a signal that suppresses the current reasoning path and up-weights alternative continuations," with the mechanism strengthening through RL; this is a form-(iii) ordering and training-regime relation coupled to causal claims. It would establish both an RL-associated phenomenon and a mechanism, predicting that detector activity precedes rerouting and jointly explains productive correction and wasteful loops—an important constraint because DeepSeek-R1 (2025, arXiv:2501.12948) attributes reasoning gains partly to emergent reflection and alternative exploration, while Stream of Search (Gandhi et al., ICLR 2024) treats backtracking as part of learned search behavior. Refutation would distinguishably rule out the proposed common detect-reroute account and its claimed RL emergence, although it would not identify the alternative mechanism; thus the branches are determinate and the negative branch remains informative. In the topic-substitution check, generic "efficient reasoning from a mechanism perspective" would not earn this score: the ordered two-stage circuit and its predicted effects on both correction and looping are specific constraints absent from the median topic-level hypothesis.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "detector-direction" and "detector-gated correction," which would provide an online intervention for invoking reconsideration or suppressing unnecessary loops. This is ex ante relative to the final answer and token expenditure: the detector is asserted to fire while a reasoning path is unfolding, leaving an action window in which a system can reroute or stop a loop rather than merely diagnose failure afterward. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive conclusion would still predict a detector-before-reroute ordering and stronger circuitry in RL-trained than base models, although it does not specify a quantitative scaling law and asserts no clear transfer across architectures or modalities; likely downstream users include reasoning-model auditors and deployment engineers who gate inference-time compute. The topic-substitution check does not preserve the score, because the topic alone supplies neither the quoted online handles nor their lead time; those claim-specific features support reach above the median.
